Analysis: Both hypotheses offer innovative perspectives on the role of AHNAK2 in liver cancer progression, but Hypothesis 2 stands out in terms of plausibility and testability. While Hypothesis 1 is highly novel by integrating multiple mechanisms (geranylgeranylation, lncRNA-driven EMT, and N‐glycosylation), its complexity renders the experimental design challenging, potentially diluting causal clarity. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 focuses more directly on the modulation of protein geranylgeranylation with a clearer cascade involving Rho/Ras GTPases and vesicular trafficking via RAB proteins. Its modular design facilitates direct testing of each step using contemporary techniques, thus enhancing its overall experimental feasibility. Both hypotheses do not raise significant safety concerns at the conceptual level, but the more focused approach of Hypothesis 2 makes it comparatively safer in terms of interpretability and translational potential.
